decisions.note: IndexedSelector (installer/mmu_types/Kconfig.vvd:3 does `select INDEXED_SELECTOR`; class extras/mmu/unit/selectors/mmu_indexed_selector.py:59): a stepper-driven gate index, not a servo -- `PARAM_SELECTOR_GEAR_RATIO` 25:10, `PARAM_SELECTOR_ROTATION_DISTANCE` 360, run/hold current 0.8/0.3 and `PARAM_SELECTOR_MOVE_SPEED` 200 (Kconfig.vvd:99-108) on the selector `[mmu_stepper]` the render names (`unit0_selector`), beside a 1:1 gear with `rotation_distance: 8.45` (Kconfig.vvd:89-90). Its working set is `selector_move_speed: 200`, `selector_accel: 1200`, `selector_gate_order: 0, 3, 1, 2` (Kconfig.vvd:84), `selector_endstop_width: 10`, plus the class's hidden CAD geometry `cad_gate_width: 90` and `cad_max_rotations: 2` (mmu_indexed_selector.py:48-49), giving a full sweep cap of `num_gates * cad_gate_width * cad_max_rotations` = 4 x 90 x 2 = 720 mm. klipper-mmu drives it as an INDEXED selector (`KLIPPER_MMU_SELECTOR_KIND_INDEXED`): a selector stepper (`KLIPPER_MMU_PINS_SELECTOR_STEP/_DIR/_ENABLE`) with one index switch per gate (`KLIPPER_MMU_PINS_SELECTOR_GATE`), no selector endstop and no servo. A selection takes the shorter way round along `KLIPPER_MMU_SELECTOR_GATE_ORDER` (`0,3,1,2`) until the gate's own switch trips, then moves half of `KLIPPER_MMU_SELECTOR_ENDSTOP_WIDTH_MM` (10 mm) further to centre on it; homing is the same search aimed at gate 0, bounded by `KLIPPER_MMU_SELECTOR_INDEXED_MAX_TRAVEL_MM` (720 mm). Software candidate: it builds and passes the simulators, but has not run on real hardware.

4 gates: `PARAM_NUM_GATES` default 4 with `DISABLE_NUM_GATES_OPTION` (installer/mmu_types/Kconfig.vvd:18 and 78) -- the gate count is fixed hardware, not user-editable. AFC knows this device (`extras/AFC_vivid.py`, `templates/AFC_Vivid_1.cfg`), and comparing its `templates/AFC_Vivid_1.cfg` with this dossier gives `lane_count: differ` (AFC's template ships 2 lanes, HH's type says 4). Where HH and AFC differ, HH's executable reference wins, so this dossier records 4. This decision exists to resolve that `differ` row.

No servo angles: the selector command is an index value. Gates are addressed in the physical order `selector_gate_order: 0, 3, 1, 2` (installer/mmu_types/Kconfig.vvd:84) -- gate 0 first, then 3, 1, 2 around the index -- and each index is found by searching a `selector_endstop_width: 10` mm window at `cad_gate_width: 90` mm spacing, over a selector axis whose `rotation_distance: 360` at the 25:10 gear ratio (Kconfig.vvd:99-101). The numbers are consistent with a 4-gate drum: 4 x 90 = 360 mm, exactly one selector revolution. klipper-mmu keeps no per-gate position table for this kind: each gate is found by its own switch on every selection, so there is nothing to calibrate per gate (`KLIPPER_MMU_CALIBRATE_SELECTOR` is refused for INDEXED); the gate order and switch width are menuconfig settings.

Arrival is the device's own buffer switch, not an extruder switch: `extruder_homing_endstop: filament_compression`, the compression side of `[mmu_buffer unit0]` (`compression_pin: unit0_buffer:PA5`, `buffer_spring_state: tension`), at layout position 711.2. LOAD runs `Homing filament to extruder endstop` on `filament_compression` (actual 21.2 mm from 690) and completes: `operations.load.end.tip = 779.2`, `filament_pos: 10`, `gate_status: 1`, `errors: []`. The final move to the nozzle is gear+extruder with no endstop, so toolhead arrival beyond the buffer is dead-reckoned; the sensed arrival is the compression switch. `[mmu_sensors unit0]` also declares per-gate entry switches (`mmu_entry_switch_pin_0..3`, unit0:PA0..PA3) and per-gate exit switches (`mmu_exit_switch_pin_0..3`, unit0_buffer:PA0..PA3), which the gate moves home on (`mmu_exit_0`) and EJECT finishes on (`mmu_entry`).

switched, and it is the device's own buffer MCU: `OPTION_VVD_BUFFER` selects `MMU_HAS_BUFFER_MCU`, `MMU_HAS_SENSOR_EXIT`, `MMU_HAS_SYNC_FEEDBACK_BUFFER`, `MMU_HAS_SENSOR_BUFFER_COMPRESSION` and `MMU_HAS_SENSOR_BUFFER_TENSION` (installer/mmu_types/Kconfig.vvd:29-34). The render records `[mmu_buffer unit0] tension_pin: unit0_buffer:PA4`, `compression_pin: unit0_buffer:PA5`, `buffer_range: 8`, `buffer_maxrange: 16`, `buffer_spring_state: tension`, with `sync_feedback_enabled: 1` and `flowguard_enabled: 1`. AFC's ViViD template agrees (`buffer_type: switched`), so this row is a plain agreement; klipper-mmu follows from a switched buffer like this one, but switched-buffer ramming remains a recorded gap, not a blocker.

PRELOAD reverse-homes off `mmu_exit_0` onto the `preload_compound` (gate switch plus NFC reader), scans `mmu_nfc_0`, reverse-homes onto `mmu_exit_0` again and then parks FORWARD: `gate_preload_parking_distance: 10` mm (Kconfig.vvd:113) past the switch, `operations.preload.end.tip = 9.999999` (`end.sensor: mmu_exit_0`, offset +10). That forward park is VVD's own default and the opposite sign of Low Rider/Pico MMU's -25.

UNLOAD retracts the bowden, reverse-homes off `mmu_exit_0` and parks +10 mm forward of it (`gate_parking_distance: 10`): `operations.unload.end.tip = 9.999999`, `gate_status: 2`. Because the park sits 10 mm past the switch, LOAD's `Initial homing to mmu_exit_0 sensor` is an already-satisfied no-op (`actual: 0.0`, `homed: true`, tip stays 9.999999); this dossier's self-consistency check accepts a no-travel homing for exactly this machine and still rejects a homing move that travelled and missed.

`gate_final_eject_distance: 800` mm (installer/mmu_types/Kconfig.vvd:115): EJECT reverse-homes off `mmu_exit_0` (10 mm) and then reverse-homes onto `mmu_entry` (layout -150, `mmu_pre_gate`) to `operations.eject.end.tip = -150.000001`, `gate_status: 0` -- the whole gate path is cleared, not the small extra retract of ERCF or MMX.

AFC cross-check `differ` row. HH's long-move speeds are `gear_load_speed: 100` mm/s and `gear_unload_speed: 80` (with `gear_load_accel`/`gear_unload_accel` 100); AFC's ViViD template declares 120/50. AFC's figure is a template default on its side, not a measured device value, and HH is the executable reference (a new device takes the number HH and AFC agree on, and HH's where they differ), so klipper-mmu's ViViD speeds follow HH.

The same AFC cross-check `differ` row for short moves: HH carries `gear_short_move_speed: 80`, `gear_short_move_accel: 400` and `gear_short_move_threshold: 70`; AFC's template says 50/300. HH wins as the executable reference.

Harness artifacts, two. (1) The compound endstop: HH builds and registers a first-wins `MmuCompoundEndstop` of [gate switch, NFC reader] on the gear rail (`_build_gate_nfc_compound`, extras/mmu/mmu_filament_movement.py), so PRELOAD's first move ends on `preload_compound`, an endstop with no single static layout position; the trace shows it converging on the gate switch at 0.0 and then re-homing on `mmu_exit_0`. This dossier's consistency check accepts a compound whose tip lands on one of its legs (`gate_homing_endstop` or the gate's `mmu_nfc` entry), and still rejects one that stopped elsewhere. (2) The NFC reader sections: the VVD board's `PARAM_MISC_HARDWARE` names its readers `unit1_nfc01`/`unit1_nfc23` (installer/boards/custom/Kconfig.vvd) because the shipped machine puts the ViViD on unit1, while a single-unit trace derives `unit0_nfc*`; the trace therefore points `PARAM_NFC_READER_0..3` at the sections the board actually emits. Reader section names and pins are board wiring, not device behaviour.
